[TAB-FULL:v20p297#2/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · بعض نحويي البصرة | reports | Some Basran grammarians treat yawm as semantically annexed to the people in it, with an understood event such as their trial; this works when yawm means idh, but otherwise is awkward. | mentions 51:13, 77:35
[TAB-FULL:v20p297#2/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · غيره | reports | Another grammarian says time words function like idh and idhā, so they retain case forms; when a pronoun returns to them, they become full nouns and take tanwīn. | mentions 11:66
[TAB-FULL:v20p297#2/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | prefers | Al-Ṭabarī prefers treating yawm and similar time expressions as adverbial particles taking the case of their syntactic position; when they appear as nouns, they accept ordinary case inflection.

[BAQILLANI:v1p198/r6] BAQILLANI, d. 403 · author | holds | The warning about the Day of Meeting leads into the scene where all are exposed, nothing is hidden from God, and the question of sovereignty is answered: it belongs to God, the One, the Subduer.
[BAQILLANI:v1p199/r4] BAQILLANI, d. 403 · author | holds | This eloquence characterizes every verse, sūra, section, story, and meaning, though narrative, law, theology, proof, and instruction each call for a different kind of speech.
